page: Microsoft Azure D2as_v7 is a general-purpose virtual machine built on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. The instance provides 2 dedicated vCPUs backed by a single physical core and two threads on an AMD EPYC 9V45 processor capable of clock speeds up to 4.5 GHz. It includes 48 KB of L1 data cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and 32 MB of L3 cache, with an instruction set supporting AVX, AVX-512, VAES, and SHA_NI extensions. Memory allocation totals 8.0 GB, maintaining a balanced 1:4 vCPU-to-memory ratio of 4.0 GB per vCPU. The server has no bundled GPU acceleration and includes no local temporary storage, requiring reliance on remote Azure Premium Storage for persistent file and operating system systems.

Benchmark data demonstrates sharp divergence between single-threaded and multi-core capabilities. In stress-ng single-core tests, the D2as_v7 places in the top tier (3584.17), paired with upper-tier throughput in single-threaded gzip compression (39.36 GB/sec) and bzip3 decompression (17.11 GB/sec). However, with only two virtual threads on one physical core, multi-core benchmarks such as PassMark CPU (4852.91) and aggregate stress-ng stay within the bottom quartile. Memory bandwidth reaches 42.68 GB/sec for uncached reads and 33.13 GB/sec for writes, both aligning with mid-range baselines, while cached reads fall lower. Throughput benchmarks for Redis (3.77 million operations per second) and static web serving (4.3 GB/sec) reflect its modest compute density.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the D2as_v7 provides access to modern AMD EPYC microarchitecture and advanced AVX-512 vector pipelines without the overhead of enterprise-scale vCPU allocations. The lack of integrated storage reduces resource waste for stateless configurations, although network-attached storage latency must be accounted for in I/O planning. This configuration is well aligned with lightweight web application hosting, staging and microservice deployments, small container runtimes, batch compression tasks, and entry-level development environments that prioritize single-thread responsiveness over parallel scaling.
description: Microsoft Azure D2as_v7 is a general-purpose virtual machine powered by an AMD EPYC 9V45 processor clocked at up to 4.5 GHz. Operating on Microsoft Hyper-V, the instance features 2 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 1 physical core, 8.0 GB of RAM, 32 MB of L3 cache, and instruction support including AVX-512 and cryptographic accelerators. It contains no onboard GPUs or local storage, operating as a diskless node compatible with remote Premium Storage. Benchmark results demonstrate top-tier single-core compute and data compression throughput, contrasted by bottom-quartile multi-core scores and modest static web and Redis performance due to its two-thread limit. Memory bandwidth remains in the mid-range with uncached read speeds of 42.68 GB/sec. D2as_v7 offers a resource-efficient option for workloads demanding high single-thread clock rates, including lightweight web serving, microservices, continuous integration tasks, and basic application hosting.
